notes: European Commission adequacy decisions under GDPR Art. 45 (and, for the UK and US, the parallel Law Enforcement Directive / DPF instruments). An entry means transfers to that destination, within the stated scope, need no additional safeguard. Transfers to destinations not listed require an Art. 46 mechanism (SCCs, BCRs, approved codes or certification) with a transfer impact assessment, or an Art. 49 derogation. The UK, US and Brazil entries are time-sensitive and marked confidence 'verify'. ukAdequacy lists the destinations the UK itself treats as adequate under the UK GDPR (Data Protection Act 2018, s.17A regulations). This file is reference data, not legal advice.

ukAdequacy.notes: Destinations the UK treats as adequate for UK GDPR transfers. The UK inherited the EU list on exit and has since added the Republic of Korea (2022), the US via the UK Extension to the EU-US DPF (the 'data bridge', in force 2023-10-12) and all EU/EEA states. Gibraltar is covered by UK legislation. The UK Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 replaces the adequacy test with a 'data protection test'; verify the current regulations.
destinations: United States (UK Extension to the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, certified organisations only)

transferMechanisms.name: Adequacy decision
transferMechanisms.notes: No further safeguard needed for transfers within the decision's scope. Still subject to the rest of the GDPR (lawful basis, transparency).

transferMechanisms.name: Standard Contractual Clauses (2021 modules)
transferMechanisms.notes: Four modules (C2C, C2P, P2P, P2C). Adopted 2021-06-04; old 2001/2010 SCCs invalid for new contracts from 2021-09-27 and for all contracts from 2022-12-27. A transfer impact assessment (Schrems II, EDPB Recommendations 01/2020) is expected alongside.

transferMechanisms.basis: UK GDPR Art. 46; ICO International Data Transfer Agreement and Addendum
transferMechanisms.name: UK IDTA / UK Addendum to the EU SCCs
transferMechanisms.notes: In force 2022-03-21. Contracts on the old EU SCCs stopped being valid for UK transfers on 2024-03-21.

transferMechanisms.name: Binding Corporate Rules
transferMechanisms.notes: Intra-group transfers; approved by the lead supervisory authority after the Art. 63 consistency mechanism. Controller and processor BCRs are separate instruments.

transferMechanisms.name: Approved codes of conduct or certification mechanisms
transferMechanisms.notes: Must be combined with binding and enforceable commitments by the importer. Few have been approved for transfers so far.

transferMechanisms.name: Ad hoc contractual clauses
transferMechanisms.notes: Bespoke clauses authorised by the competent supervisory authority.

transferMechanisms.name: Derogations for specific situations
transferMechanisms.notes: Explicit consent, contract performance, important public interest, legal claims, vital interests, public register, or (last resort) compelling legitimate interests for non-repetitive limited transfers. Occasional use only; not a basis for systematic transfers (EDPB Guidelines 2/2018).
